Reference

ABI major versions

This page states what happens when the plugin contract moves from the 0.x line to 1.0.0. The rules on the ABI evolution page apply inside each major line: a minor release adds only, keeps a window of the current minor and the previous one, and refuses what falls outside it. A major release is the one point where a change may break the rules of that page. This page says which 0.x minors stay loadable across that point, how a package is refused across it, and what a major release may change.

Terms

  • Major boundary. The release that moves the first number of api (the contract version ilium:plugin@MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) from 0 to 1.
  • Final 0.x minor. The highest 0.N minor released before 1.0.0. The number is not fixed on this page; it is whatever the last 0.x release is.
  • Frozen copy and adapter. The kept wit/since_v0_N/ copy of a minor and the hand-written adapter the host reads it through, as defined on ABI evolution.
  • Removal major. The major release in which a marked feature or the retained 0.x minor stops working.

What you need

  • The ABI evolution rules. The window, the refusal codes and the removal notice are defined on ABI evolution. This page refers to them and does not repeat them.
  • The versioning rules for authors. Versioning explains the api key and the ilium:api-version section from the author side.

1. The version written at a major boundary

The three places that carry the contract version are the same as in every minor release: the manifest key api, the custom section ilium:api-version and the @ suffix of the WIT package names. At 1.0.0 the three places hold ilium:plugin@1.0.0. The custom section of a 1.0.0 component is the three big-endian u16 values 1, 0 and 0, so its bytes are 00 01 00 00 00 00. A component whose section differs from its manifest api is refused with manifest.api-version, the same as in a minor release.

A component built for 1.0.0 and a component built for 0.x are never the same binary. A plugin author rebuilds the component with the SDK of the new major to target 1.0.0.

  • [ABI-059] A component built for ilium:plugin@1.0.0 MUST carry the custom section ilium:api-version with bytes 00 01 00 00 00 00, and a section that differs from the manifest api MUST be refused with manifest.api-version.

2. The 0.x minor that stays loadable

A host that ships 1.0.0 keeps the final 0.x minor loadable for a limited time. The host reads that minor through its frozen copy and an adapter, the same way it reads the previous minor inside the window.

  • [ABI-055] A host that ships ilium:plugin@1.0.0 MUST load a package whose api is the final 0.x minor through that minor's frozen copy and adapter, and MUST NOT load a package whose api is any other 0.x minor.

Decision needed: how long the final 0.x minor stays loadable after 1.0.0 is released. The default I would use is until the next major release, under the same window rule that applies to minors, so a plugin author has one full major cycle to rebuild. The owner should confirm this period before the 1.0.0 release is announced.

  • [ABI-950] The final 0.x minor MUST stay loadable until 12 months (proposed, owner to confirm) after the release of 2.0.0, which is the end point of the default above. After that date a package whose api is that minor MUST be refused with package.api-unsupported under [ABI-056]. The owner is the project maintainer who signs the 1.0.0 release (proposed, owner to confirm), and the owner MUST state the date in the release notes of 1.0.0.

Inputs are the api key of the manifest and the ilium:api-version section of the component. The output of the check is either a loaded package or one refusal code.

3. Refusal across the major boundary

A package whose api names a major version that the host does not load is refused at install, at stage 3, with package.api-unsupported. The refusal uses the same table and the same order as a minor refusal, so the host reports one code for each package.

  • [ABI-056] A package whose api major differs from the host's major version and whose api is not the one retained under [ABI-055] MUST be refused with package.api-unsupported, and the message MUST name the api of the package and the versions the host supports.

A 1.0.0 package on a 0.x host is refused with package.api-unsupported in the same way, because 1.0.0 is outside the window of every 0.x host. A 0.x package that is not the final minor is refused on a 1.0.0 host with the same code.

Package api Host 1.0.0 Host 0.x
ilium:plugin@1.0.0 loads package.api-unsupported
final 0.x minor loads, one deprecated record loads if inside the host window
other 0.x minor package.api-unsupported loads if inside the host window
not a well-formed string manifest.schema manifest.schema
section differs from api manifest.api-version manifest.api-version

Failure behaviour: the host reports the first failing check in the order of the table on ABI evolution, so one package gets one code. A refused install changes nothing on disk.

4. Deprecation of the 0.x line

The retained 0.x minor is a deprecated feature line. The host reports that state at load time, with the same record that a marked feature uses.

  • [ABI-057] The host MUST log one deprecated record per plugin when it loads a package whose api is the final 0.x minor, and the record MUST name the major version in which that 0.x minor stops loading.

5. What a major release may change

A minor release may only add. A major release is the only release that may change the contract in ways a minor release may not. The table on ABI evolution lists the fixed parts; a major release may change them only under the rules below.

  • [ABI-058] A major release MUST NOT lower a limit or remove a feature unless the change was marked in an earlier release under [ABI-052] and [ABI-053], and the change MUST take effect in that major release only.

A limit may be lowered only in a major version. A removal follows the same notice rule as a minor removal, with the removal minor replaced by the removal major. The affected package refusals move to the codes of ABI evolution under [ABI-054].

Decision needed: how much notice a feature removal needs before a major release. The default I would use is the two-minor notice of [ABI-052], which means the feature is marked in a minor release at least two minors before the major release that removes it. A shorter notice would leave plugin authors less time to rebuild, so the default is the longer one.

6. Inside the 1.x line

After the boundary the rules of ABI evolution apply again to 1.N minors: a minor only adds, and the host loads the current minor and the previous one.

  • [ABI-060] Inside the 1.x line a host MUST apply the window rule of ABI evolution (current minor and previous one), and a package whose api major differs from the host's major MUST NOT be loaded through that window.

End of a major line

  • [ABI-951] For each major line N from 1 onward, the host MUST keep the final minor of major N loadable through its frozen copy and adapter, as [ABI-055] does for 0.x, until 12 months (proposed, owner to confirm) after the release of major N+1. After that date the host MUST refuse packages of major N with package.api-unsupported under [ABI-056], and the release notes of major N+1 MUST state that date.

Limits

  • Retained 0.x minors on a 1.0.0 host: exactly one (the final minor) [ABI-055].
  • deprecated records: one per plugin per load [ABI-057].
  • Notice for a removal: at least two minors before the removal major, as the default of the decision above; the number is not settled until the owner confirms it.
  • A patch change moves no interface and never affects these rules.

Example

A host at 1.0.0 whose final 0.x minor is 0.3.0 (illustrative numbers):

  • old.plugin with api = "ilium:plugin@0.3.0" loads and logs one deprecated record naming the removal major.
  • older.plugin with api = "ilium:plugin@0.2.0" is refused with package.api-unsupported; the message names ilium:plugin@0.2.0 and the supported versions.
  • new.plugin with api = "ilium:plugin@1.0.0" and section bytes 00 01 00 00 00 00 loads.

7. What an author sees

  • A plugin built for 1.0.0 loads on a 1.0.0 host.
  • A plugin built for the final 0.x minor loads on a 1.0.0 host, logs one deprecated record at load, and is refused after the removal major.
  • A plugin built for any other 0.x minor is refused with package.api-unsupported on a 1.0.0 host.

What this page does not cover

  • The window, refusal table and removal notice inside one major line: ABI evolution.
  • How authors write and check the api key: Versioning.
  • Upgrade steps for plugin authors and operators: Compatibility and upgrades.
  • The full list of rules and tests: Requirements for WIT and ABI.

Operator procedure for ABI incompatibility

Target behaviour of the production plugin system.

  • [ABI-076] The page MUST give a runbook for an operator whose host upgrade makes installed plugins refuse with package.api-unsupported or a section mismatch, covering triage, pin, roll back and bulk report in that order.
  • [ABI-077] The host MUST provide a command that lists every installed plugin refused for an ABI reason, with the refusal code and the plugin's declared api, in one output.
  • [ABI-078] Rolling the host back MUST NOT change installed plugin files, grants or stored settings, and a plugin refused after the upgrade MUST load again unchanged after the rollback.

See also

  • ABI evolution
  • Versioning
  • Compatibility and upgrades
  • Requirements for WIT and ABI

Production additions: T9-compat-deprecation

  • [DEV-964] The project MUST support each host minor release with security fixes for at least 12 months (proposed, owner to confirm) after its release date and MUST publish that end date in the support matrix at release time; the window of ABI minors (current and previous) is a loading rule and MUST NOT be read as the support period.
  • [DEV-966] A fix for a vulnerability in the plugin host, sandbox or SDK MUST be released as a patch to every host minor still inside its support period (DEV-964), and a patch release MUST NOT change any WIT interface, limit, error code or manifest key.
  • [DEV-995] A major host release MUST be announced in the release notes of a minor at least 6 months (proposed, owner to confirm) before its release date, with the list of every removal and limit change it contains; the announced list MUST NOT grow after the announcement.
  • [DEV-962] The support matrix MUST list every host minor release in one row, with its release date, its security-fix end date from [DEV-964] and its support state. The state MUST read supported up to that end date and end-of-life after it, as [DEV-965] reports it. A row MUST NOT be removed when its minor reaches the end date. An installed plugin on an end-of-life minor MUST keep loading unchanged, because the end date limits security fixes and not loading.

Example row (illustrative only):

Host minor Released Security fixes until Support
0.3.0 2026-01-15 2027-01-15 supported until that date

Requirement statements

  • [ABI-055] A host that ships ilium:plugin@1.0.0 MUST load a package whose api is the final 0.x minor through that minor's frozen copy and adapter, and MUST NOT load a package whose api is any other 0.x minor.
  • [ABI-056] A package whose api major differs from the host's major and is not the retained 0.x minor MUST be refused with package.api-unsupported, and the message MUST name the package's api and the supported versions.
  • [ABI-057] The host MUST log one deprecated record per plugin when it loads the final 0.x minor, naming the major version in which that minor stops loading.
  • [ABI-058] A major release MUST NOT lower a limit or remove a feature unless the change was marked in an earlier release under ABI-052 and ABI-053, and the change MUST take effect in that major release only.
  • [ABI-059] A component built for ilium:plugin@1.0.0 MUST carry the custom section ilium:api-version with bytes 00 01 00 00 00 00, and a section that differs from the manifest api MUST be refused with manifest.api-version.
  • [ABI-060] Inside the 1.x line a host MUST apply the window rule of ABI evolution (current minor and previous one), and a package whose api major differs from the host's major MUST NOT be loaded through that window.
  • [ABI-076] The page MUST give a runbook for an operator whose host upgrade makes installed plugins refuse with package.api-unsupported or a section mismatch, covering triage, pin, roll back and bulk report in that order.
  • [ABI-077] The host MUST provide a command that lists every installed plugin refused for an ABI reason, with the refusal code and the plugin's declared api, in one output.
  • [ABI-078] Rolling the host back MUST NOT change installed plugin files, grants or stored settings, and a plugin refused after the upgrade MUST load again unchanged after the rollback.
  • [ABI-950] The final 0.x minor MUST stay loadable until 12 months (proposed, owner to confirm) after the release of 2.0.0, and after that date a package whose api is that minor MUST be refused with package.api-unsupported.
  • [ABI-951] For each major line N from 1 onward, the host MUST keep the final minor of major N loadable through its frozen copy and adapter until 12 months (proposed, owner to confirm) after the release of major N+1, then MUST refuse packages of major N with package.api-unsupported, and the release notes of major N+1 MUST state that date.
